newsitem.title: USA: DAKA sees Q1, Q2 results trailing 1996.
newsitem.headline: DAKA sees Q1, Q2 results trailing 1996.

text.p: DAKA International Inc expects earnings in the first and second quarters of fiscal 1997 to be lower than those reported for the same periods of fiscal 1996, company officials told analysts in a conference call Monday.

Elaborating on the company's earlier projection that it would earn $0.70 to $0.80 per share in the current year, the officials estimated a first-quarter loss of $0.10 to $0.12 per share, followed by a second-quarter profit of $0.18 to $0.21.
In the first quarter of fiscal 1996, the company earned $0.22 per share. In the second, it earned $0.36, $0.20 in the third and $0.03 in the fourth quarter, ended June 29.
Management told analysts they project third quarter 1997 earnings of $0.31 to $0.33 per share and fourth quarter earnings of $0.33 to $0.36 per share.

Noting the drop from the $1.25 per share for 1997 it was talking about in July, DAKA's management cited two items of overhead -- corporate and the venture being discussed with K Mart Corp -- for $0.10 per share of the decline and higher interest rates for about $0.20.
Chief Executive William H. Baumhauer said the continued decline in Fuddruckers results in July and August left this segment "moderately worse" than it was in the fourth quarter.
Sales at company-owned Fuddruckers accounted for $132 million of DAKA's $218 million in total 1996 sales.
Baumhauer cited declining operating standards, a inadequate marketing strategy and below-average results in Fuddruckers with the company's new design for the segment's problems.
He said the marketing vice president has been replaced and new ads will begin airing this month.
Expansion has been curtailed to 10 to 15 units in fiscal 1997 from the 30 planned previously, and the prototype is being redesigned, Baumhauer said.
Later, the CEO said he would "guess 12 or 13 new units" will be added this year.
He said the Mexican food and pizza added to the menu of some of DAKA's Fuddruckers had not added as much to profit margins as the company had hoped and were being looked at again.
If the company decided to continue with those concepts, Baumhauer said, the results would be additive to the $0.70 to $0.80 per share it was now projecting for fiscal 1997.
He also said the company has curtailed its planned Champps expansions to 10 to 15 new stores this year from the 15 to 20 projected earlier.

Baumhauer said DAKA did not sign a contract with Kmart by September 1 as expected because of problems in turning the tentative agreement into a definitive agreement to operate the retail chain's in-store restaurants.
There are "significant issues" remaining to be settled, he said, adding "hopefully" he will know in the next couple of weeks whether an agreement was possible..
